q: Can an NBFC lend me green deposit money for a solar or efficiency project?
title: NBFC green deposit loans for MSME projects
short: Yes, if the NBFC takes deposits and your project is on RBI's green list, such as solar, LED lighting, efficiency retrofits or electric vehicles. RBI's 2025 directions for deposit-taking NBFCs and housing finance companies send green deposit money only to listed green activities, and an NBFC may also fund green projects without green deposits.
audience: MSME owners borrowing from an NBFC for a green project, and NBFC credit officers

p: The Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies: Climate Finance and Management of Climate Change Risks) Directions, 2025, dated 28 November 2025, apply to deposit-taking NBFCs and deposit-taking housing finance companies. Raising green deposits is optional. An NBFC that does not take deposits is outside these directions, though it can still lend for your solar plant on its own terms.

sections.h: Projects green deposit money can fund
ul: Renewable energy: solar, wind, biomass and hydropower projects that pair generation with storage, and support for adopting renewable energy.
Energy efficiency: efficient systems in buildings, LED lighting replacements, efficiency retrofits and new low-carbon buildings.
Clean transport: electric vehicles and charging infrastructure.
Water and waste: wastewater treatment, water conservation, waste recycling and reduction, and pollution control.
Not eligible: projects whose core energy source is fossil fuel, biomass from protected areas, landfills, direct waste incineration and hydro plants above 25 MW, among others.

p: An NBFC may not finance a project first and then raise green deposits for it afterwards. So if you want your loan to sit in the NBFC's green deposit book, raise it before sanction. A loan already disbursed cannot be funded from green deposits raised afterwards.

sections.h: What the NBFC has to check, and will ask you for
ul: Its Board-approved Financing Framework covers how it evaluates and selects projects and how it validates the information the borrower provides. The framework, with an external reviewer's opinion, must be on its website, so you can read the eligibility rules yourself.
An independent third party checks every year that green deposit money went to eligible projects.
The NBFC must assess the impact of its green lending yearly, with indicators such as MWh of energy saved or generated and tonnes of CO2e avoided per project. Expect to be asked for those numbers.
RBI defines greenwashing as marketing something as green when it does not meet these requirements. A loan with no evidence behind its green label is a risk for the lender, not just for you.

example.title: LED retrofit plus 100 kW of rooftop solar
lines: LED saving from your bills and the supplier's figures: 40,000 kWh a year (assumed)
Solar output: 100 kW x 1,400 kWh per kW (assumed yield) = 1,40,000 kWh a year
Energy figure the NBFC reports: 40,000 + 1,40,000 = 1,80,000 kWh, or 180 MWh
CO2e avoided: 1,80,000 kWh x 0.675 kg per kWh (CEA grid factor, FY 2025-26) = 1,21,500 kg, about 121.5 tonnes a year
example.note: These are the two impact figures the directions use as examples. Give them as estimates at sanction, then replace them with figures from your bills after a year of running.

senseible: Senseible reads your electricity bills before and after the project into kWh and CO2 per month, the impact figures an NBFC's yearly assessment asks for. The green loan readiness check shows which ones you still lack. Senseible does not lend, and its records are not a third-party review.
